problems.title: An odd number of nested subtractions
problems.question: Find $A=-x-(1-(1-(1-\dots(1-x)\dots)))$ when 1 occurs 101 times.
problems.idea: The transformation T(u)=1-u reverses itself after two applications.
steps: The 100 innermost paired applications return x.
One remaining application makes the bracket 1-x.
Therefore A=-x-(1-x)=-1.

problems.title: When a linear equation is impossible
problems.question: For which k does $(k^2+k-12)x=k+4$ have no solution?
problems.idea: The x-coefficient must vanish while the other side stays nonzero.
formulas: Ax=B has no solution iff A=0 and B≠0.
steps: Factor k²+k-12=(k+4)(k-3).
At k=-4 both sides are zero, giving infinitely many solutions.
At k=3 the equation is 0·x=7, impossible.

problems.title: Factor by grouping a numerical expression
problems.question: Evaluate $38.4^2-61.6\cdot29.5+61.6\cdot38.4-29.5\cdot38.4$.
problems.idea: Group terms into a common sum and difference.
formulas: a²+ab-ac-bc=(a+b)(a-c).
steps: Then a+b=100 and a-c=8.9.
The expression equals 100·8.9=890.

problems.title: Two arrival times reveal the distance
problems.question: At 15 km/h a cyclist arrives 10 minutes before a bus departs; at 12 km/h the cyclist would arrive 5 minutes late. Find the distance.
problems.idea: The slower journey lasts 15 minutes longer.
formulas: Time=distance/speed; 15 minutes=1/4 hour.
steps: For distance d, d/12-d/15=1/4.
The left coefficient is (5-4)/60=1/60.
Thus d/60=1/4, so d=15.

problems.title: Distinguish the minimizer from the minimum
problems.question: Find x for which $x^2-0.6x+2$ is smallest.
problems.idea: Complete the square and read where it is zero.
steps: The squared term is always nonnegative.
It becomes zero precisely at x=0.3.
The minimum value is 1.91, but the requested x is 0.3.
problems.note: The choices list 1.91 but omit x=0.3. The listed value answers a different question from the one printed.

problems.title: A denominator that never vanishes
problems.question: For which b is $2/(x^2+2x+b)$ defined for every real x?
problems.idea: Complete the denominator’s square.
steps: If b>1, the denominator is always at least b-1>0.
If b=1, it vanishes at x=-1.
If b<1, choose x=-1±√(1-b) to make it zero.

problems.title: Two points with the same height on a parabola
problems.question: A(a,0.36) lies on y=x². Find a.
problems.idea: Substitute the coordinates and take both square roots.
formulas: a²=c>0 gives a=±√c.
steps: The condition gives a²=0.36.
Since 0.6²=0.36, both a=0.6 and a=-0.6 work.

problems.title: Order powers of a negative fraction
problems.question: Order a,a²,a³,a⁴,a⁵ increasingly when -1<a<0.
problems.idea: Separate negative odd powers from positive even powers.
formulas: For 0<t<1, higher positive powers have smaller magnitude.
steps: The odd powers are negative; the even powers are positive.
Among the odd powers, a is most negative, then a³, then a⁵.
Among the even powers, a⁴<a².
Combining gives a<a³<a⁵<a⁴<a².

problems.title: Factor a positive-integer equation
problems.question: Find x+y for positive integers satisfying xy-2x+3y+1=0.
problems.idea: Add and subtract the constant needed for a product.
steps: The equation becomes (x+3)(y-2)=-7.
Since x+3≥4, its only possible positive divisor of 7 is 7.
Thus x+3=7 and y-2=-1, giving x=4,y=1.

problems.title: Simplify a fractional system before solving
problems.question: Find a+b if $\frac{2(a-3b)}3-\frac{b+4}2-\frac{2a-3}6=-\frac43$, $-\frac{3(b-2a)}4-3=\frac{2a-10+b}4$.
problems.idea: Clear each equation’s denominators.
formulas: Multiplying all terms by the same nonzero number preserves solutions.
steps: Multiply the first by 6 to get 4a-12b-3b-12-2a+3=-8, hence 2a-15b=1.
Multiply the second by 4: -3b+6a-12=2a-10+b, hence a-b=1/2.
Substitute a=b+1/2 into the first: -13b=0, so b=0 and a=1/2.

problems.title: Locate an apartment number
problems.question: A building has 12 floors and 4 apartments per floor in each entrance. In which entrance and floor is apartment 87?
problems.idea: Each entrance contains 48 apartments; count from the first apartment in the second entrance.
formulas: Apartments per entrance=12·4=48.
steps: Numbers 1–48 are in entrance 1; numbers 49–96 are in entrance 2.
Within entrance 2, apartment 87 is number 87-48=39.
Floors contain groups of four; floor 10 contains within-entrance numbers 37–40.

problems.title: Recover two line equations from the graph
problems.question: Find the sum of the coordinates of the intersection of the two lines in the source graph.
problems.idea: Read two exact grid points on each line, then solve their equations.
formulas: Slope=(change in y)/(change in x); y=mx+b.
steps: The rising line passes through (-2,-1) and (2,2), so y=3x/4+1/2.
The descending line passes through (-1,2) and (2,1), so y=-x/3+5/3.
Equate: 3x/4+1/2=-x/3+5/3. Multiplying by 12 gives 13x=14.
Thus x=14/13 and y=17/13; their sum is 31/13.

problems.title: Parallel lines retain their slope
problems.question: Line a is 3x-5y+7=0; b∥a and c∥b. Line c has y-intercept -3. Find c.
problems.idea: All three parallel lines have the same slope.
formulas: A nonvertical line y=mx+b has slope m and y-intercept b.
steps: Rearrange a as y=(3/5)x+7/5, so its slope is 3/5.
Line c has that same slope and intercept -3.
Therefore c is y=0.6x-3.

problems.title: Separate two filling rates
problems.question: Two pipes together fill a tank in 80 minutes. Ten minutes of the first and 12 minutes of the second fill 2/15 of the tank. Find the first pipe’s solo time.
problems.idea: Measure both rates in tanks per minute.
formulas: If rates are u,v, then u+v=1/80 and work=rate·time.
steps: We have 10u+12v=2/15.
One full tank takes 120 minutes.

problems.title: Translate a line with a known displacement
problems.question: The translation sends A(-2,5) to B(3,1). Find the image of 4x-2y=5.
problems.idea: Use the displacement (5,-4) for every point.
formulas: For (X,Y)=(x+h,y+k), substitute x=X-h,y=Y-k.
steps: Here x=X-5,y=Y+4.
Substitute: 4(X-5)-2(Y+4)=5, giving 4X-2Y=33.
Therefore Y=2X-16.5.

problems.title: Two division points on one segment
problems.question: C divides AB in ratio 3:7 from A; D divides it in ratio 7:8 from B. CD=14 cm. Find AB.
problems.idea: Express both positions as fractions measured from A.
formulas: If AC:CB=p:q, then AC=p·AB/(p+q).
steps: Let AB=L. Then AC=3L/10.
Since BD:DA=7:8, AD=8L/15.

problems.title: A reflection creates two possible side lengths
problems.question: Through A and C draw lines perpendicular to the bisector of B, meeting lines CB and AB at K and M respectively. BM=8 cm and KC=1 cm. Find AB.
problems.idea: Reflection in the angle bisector interchanges the two side rays.
formulas: A chord between the two rays perpendicular to their bisector has endpoints equally far from B.
steps: The reflection of C is M, so BC=BM=8. Likewise AB=BK.
Both C and K lie on ray BC, but their order is not given. Thus KC=|BK-BC|=|AB-8|.
Solve |AB-8|=1 to get AB=7 or AB=9.
problems.answer: AB=7 cm or 9 cm; only 7 cm appears among the choices.
problems.note: The source does not say whether K lies between B and C or beyond C. Both side lengths satisfy the given construction.

problems.title: Hypotenuse segments from a 30-degree leg
problems.question: A right triangle has a 30° angle and hypotenuse 8 cm. The altitude from the right angle splits the hypotenuse. Find both pieces.
problems.idea: Find the shorter leg, then use its projection formula.
formulas: The 30°-opposite leg=c/2; leg²=hypotenuse·adjacent hypotenuse projection.
steps: The short leg is 8/2=4 cm.
Its projection is 4²/8=2 cm.
The other projection is 8-2=6 cm.

problems.title: Tangent lengths on a triangle side
problems.question: A triangle has side lengths a,b,c. Find the two pieces into which the incircle’s contact point divides side b.
problems.idea: Equal tangent lengths from each vertex form three linear equations.
formulas: With semiperimeter s=(a+b+c)/2, the tangent lengths at the ends of side b are s-a and s-c.
steps: Let side b be AC, side a=BC and side c=AB.
If the tangent lengths from A,B,C are u,v,w, then u+v=c,v+w=a,u+w=b.
Adding the first and third and subtracting the second gives 2u=b+c-a.
The other piece is w=b-u=(a+b-c)/2.

problems.title: Angle between altitudes in an isosceles triangle
problems.question: In an isosceles triangle, the angle between an altitude to the base and an altitude to a leg, plus the apex angle, is 105°. Find the apex angle.
problems.idea: The acute angle between the altitude lines equals a base angle.
formulas: Angles between perpendicular lines equal the corresponding acute angles between the original lines.
steps: Let the apex angle be α and each base angle β=(180°-α)/2.
The two altitude lines are perpendicular to the base and a leg, so their acute angle is β.
Thus α/2=15° and α=30°.

problems.title: Centre-triangle perimeter cancels the small radius
problems.question: Two equal circles touch each other and internally touch a larger circle. Their centre triangle has perimeter 24 cm. Find the large radius.
problems.idea: Write its three side lengths in terms of R and r.
formulas: Centre distances at tangency are R-r internally and 2r externally.
steps: The sides are R-r,R-r,2r.
Their sum is 2(R-r)+2r=2R.
Therefore 2R=24, so R=12.

problems.title: Angles in the incircle contact triangle
problems.question: A triangle has angles 40°,80°,60°. Find the largest angle of the triangle formed by its incircle contact points.
problems.idea: Each contact-triangle angle is half an arc opposite an original vertex.
formulas: The contact arc at vertex A has measure 180°-A, so its opposite inscribed angle is 90°-A/2.
steps: The three contact-triangle angles are 90°-20°=70°, 90°-40°=50°, and 90°-30°=60°.
Their sum is 180°, checking the result.
The largest is 70°.

problems.title: Incircle contact ratios in a right triangle
problems.question: The incircle divides the two legs in ratios 1:5 and 2:3, measured from the right-angle vertex. Its radius is 4 cm. Find the hypotenuse.
problems.idea: Both tangent segments from the right-angle vertex equal the inradius.
formulas: Equal tangents from a vertex have equal lengths; in a right angle, the tangent length from the vertex is r.
steps: For ratio 1:5, the first leg has pieces 4 and 20, so length 24.
For ratio 2:3, the second has pieces 4 and 6, so length 10.
The hypotenuse is the sum of the other tangent lengths, 20+6=26.

problems.title: Include the collinear boundary case
problems.question: For three points A,B,C in the plane, AB=8.3 and AC=4.9. Which listed value cannot equal BC?
problems.idea: The points are not required to form a nondegenerate triangle.
formulas: |AB-AC|≤BC≤AB+AC, with equality possible for collinear points.
steps: The distance bounds are 3.4≤BC≤13.2.
The listed 13.2 is possible when A lies between B and C.
The listed 13.3 exceeds the maximum and cannot occur.

problems.title: Centres bisect the angles between common tangents
problems.question: Two circles touch externally at K. Their common tangent at K meets an external common tangent AB at M. Find angle O₁MO₂.
problems.idea: Each circle centre lies on a bisector of the angle formed by its two tangents from M.
formulas: Equal tangent lengths and equal radii make the centre-to-M line an angle bisector.
steps: The two circles lie on opposite sides of the tangent at K.
The angles between the tangent rays containing the respective circles are supplementary: call them θ and 180°-θ.
Their centre lines bisect those angles, so the angle between the centres from M is θ/2+(180°-θ)/2=90°.
